habitat: Pairs in bushveld, grassland, pastures and cultivated fields. It usually flushes with reluctance.
summary: Newman calls it a common resident and visitor. Pale underparts in both sexes. Above rufous, mottled and streaked black and white, with white head markings, a dark throat, pale rufous underparts and white-streaked flanks. In flight it is difficult to tell from Harlequin Quail. When breeding it calls whit-WHIttit, whit-WHIttit, rendered wet-my-lips, by day or night. If flushed it calls pree-pree-pree. Status and months are unset. No Kruger photograph. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: The Harlequin Quail account printed on the Crested Francolin page says the male is darker, with black markings on a white throat and chestnut underparts.

calls.description: When breeding, a penetrating whit-WHIttit, whit-WHIttit, rendered wet-my-lips, by day or night. If flushed, pree-pree-pree. Grade A call from Furnes, Hedmark, Norway. The only South African grade A has a Cloud Cisticola in the background. The filename is XC137862-Vaktel XC -Høsbjør - 09.06.2013 kl. 13.00 1.mp3.
